blocks.html: By default, C++ runs statements one after another from top to bottom. This is sequential flow. Real programs need to make decisions ("if the password is correct, open the account") and repeat work ("send an SMS to all 500 students"). The order in which statements run is called the flow of control.

blocks.html: (a) for loop — used when the number of repetitions is known.
Order: initialisation (once) → check condition → body → update → check condition → … until the condition is false.
(b) while loop — an entry-controlled loop; the condition is checked before the body. Used when the number of repetitions is not known in advance.

Loop practice: Print (a) the multiplication table of any number, (b) all even numbers between 1 and 100, (c) the sum of the series 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + … + 1/n.

blocks.html: 1. Differentiate between while and do-while .
Answer: while checks the condition first (entry-controlled) and may run 0 times. do- while runs the body first and checks the condition after (exit-controlled), so it runs at least once.
2. Differentiate between break and continue .
Answer: break ends the loop completely and control goes to the statement after the loop. continue skips only the remaining statements of the current iteration and starts the next iteration.
3. Rewrite using a while loop:

blocks.code: for (int i = 10; i >= 1; i--) cout << i << " ";

blocks.html: 4. Write the output:

blocks.code: for (int k = 10; k > 0; k /= 2) cout << k << " ";

blocks.html: Answer: 10 5 2 1 (10 → 5 → 2 → 1 → 0 stops).
5. What is a nested loop? Give an example.
Answer: A loop inside another loop. For each iteration of the outer loop, the inner loop runs fully. Example: printing a multiplication grid with for (i...) for (j...) cout << i * j; .
6. Why is default used in switch ?
Answer: default runs when no case matches the expression. It is used to handle invalid input, e.g. "Invalid choice".
